tools.name: add_obstacle
tools.description: Add an obstacle (solid block) to the FDS model. XB=[x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2] in metres.

tools.name: remove_obstacle
tools.description: Remove an obstacle by ID.

tools.name: update_obstacle
tools.description: Update an existing obstacle by ID. Provide only fields to change.

tools.name: set_fds_properties
tools.description: Update an obstacle's Runtime FDS Properties. Merge ANY fds_override fields and/or set is_fire_source/hrrpua/surf_ids. fds_override examples — fire: hrrpua_override, tmp_front, ramp_points, fire_area, fire_faces, ext_coeff; fuel/REAC: fuel_type, reac_co_yield, reac_soot_yield, reac_hcn_yield, reac_radiative_fraction; heat detector: activation_temp, rti, initial_temp; smoke: alpha_e, beta_e, alpha_c, beta_c; thermocouple: bead_diameter, emissivity, tc_density, specific_heat; sprinkler: spr_temp, spr_rti, c_factor, flow_rate, offset, jet_velocity, spray_angle, particle_diameter, monodisperse, spr_activation_time, spr_orientation; HVAC: hvac_direction, volume_flow_rate, temperature, velocity, fan_curve, face_surfs, ramp_up_time. Read current values first with get_object_properties.

fds_override.description: fds_override fields to merge (any of the documented keys).

tools.name: add_hole
tools.description: Add a hole (opening in an obstacle) to the FDS model. XB defines the hole volume.

tools.name: remove_hole
tools.description: Remove a hole by ID.

tools.name: update_hole
tools.description: Update an existing hole by ID.

tools.name: add_wall
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a wall by specifying start point, end point, height, and thickness. Automatically calculates the OBST bounding box. Points are [x,y] on the floor plane.

tools.name: add_floor
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a floor slab. Specify x/y range and optional thickness.

tools.name: add_door
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a door opening in a wall. Specify the wall obstacle ID and door position/size. Creates a HOLE that cuts through the wall.

wall_id.description: ID of the wall obstacle to cut

position.description: Position along the wall as fraction 0-1 (default 0.5 = center)

tools.name: add_window
tools.description: Convenience tool: add a window opening in a wall. Similar to add_door but with sill height.

wall_id.description: ID of the wall obstacle to cut

tools.name: transform_obstacle
tools.description: Move / resize / rotate an existing obstacle (the 3D gizmo + property-panel SX/SY/SZ of the GUI). move = relative offset [dx,dy,dz] (m); place_at = absolute target point for `anchor` (default the XB centre); scale = absolute per-axis scale factors that stretch XB about its centre and rescale furniture voxels; rotation = [rx,ry,rz] degrees (kept as GUI metadata — &OBST itself stays axis-aligned, so a rotated furniture item is exported through its voxels). Combine as many as you need in one call.

anchor.description: place_at reference: 'center' (default), 'min' (XB min corner), 'base' (XY centre at z_min)

tools.name: list_geoms
tools.description: List the &GEOM (triangulated cut-cell geometry) entries in the deck with triangle count, SURF_ID and bounding box.

tools.name: remove_geom
tools.description: Remove a &GEOM entry by ID (see list_geoms).

tools.name: add_fire
tools.description: Add a fire source. HRRPUA = Heat Release Rate Per Unit Area (kW/m²). XB defines location. For a time-varying fire, pass ramp_points (an explicit HRR fraction curve) OR growth (an NFPA t-squared growth curve) — both auto-create a RAMP and link it.

hrrpua.description: Peak heat release rate per unit area (kW/m²)

ramp_id.description: Optional explicit RAMP ID. If omitted and a curve is given, one is auto-generated.

ramp_points.description: Time-varying HRR curve as [[time_s, fraction], ...] where fraction is 0–1 of HRRPUA. Auto-creates a RAMP.

growth.description: NFPA t-squared fire growth preset. Auto-generates a RAMP rising as (t/t_peak)^2 to full HRRPUA.

time_to_peak.description: Seconds to reach full HRRPUA when using growth (defaults by preset: slow 600, medium 300, fast 150, ultrafast 75).

tools.name: update_fire
tools.description: Update an existing fire source by index (0-based).

tools.name: remove_fire
tools.description: Remove a fire source by index (0-based).

tools.name: update_reaction
tools.description: Update the combustion reaction parameters.

tools.name: add_species
tools.description: Add a tracked species.

tools.name: remove_species
tools.description: Remove a tracked species by ID.

tools.name: add_vent
tools.description: Add a vent (boundary patch). XB defines the vent surface.

tools.name: remove_vent
tools.description: Remove a vent by ID.

tools.name: update_vent
tools.description: Update an existing vent by ID.

tools.name: set_open_boundary
tools.description: Set a domain face as OPEN (or close it). Face: XMIN, XMAX, YMIN, YMAX, ZMIN, ZMAX.

tools.name: set_all_boundaries_open
tools.description: Set all 6 domain faces to OPEN (or selectively by providing a list of faces).

tools.name: add_device
tools.description: Add a measurement device (&DEVC) with full parameter support: point (xyz) or region (xb) quantities, species, statistics, trip options (setpoint/latch/initial_state/trip_direction), post-processing, aspiration, HVAC and particle quantities. Provide xyz for point quantities or xb for flow/HRR/layer/beam/statistics.

quantity.description: FDS QUANTITY (e.g. TEMPERATURE, VOLUME FRACTION, MASS FLOW +, LAYER HEIGHT, PATH OBSCURATION, HRR, CONTROL)

xb.description: Region [x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2] — plane for flow, box for HRR/statistics, segment for beam, column for layer

spec_id.description: Species: OXYGEN, CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON MONOXIDE, SOOT, WATER VAPOR, or fuel name

setpoint.description: Trip threshold (device acts as trigger when crossed)

ctrl_id.description: CTRL reference (required for QUANTITY=CONTROL / CONTROL VALUE)

spatial_statistic.description: MEAN, MAX, MIN, VOLUME MEAN/INTEGRAL, MASS MEAN/INTEGRAL, AREA INTEGRAL, SUM, VOLUME, MASS (needs xb)

temporal_statistic.description: TIME AVERAGE, RUNNING AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, MAX TIME, MIN TIME, TIME INTEGRAL, RMS, COV, CORRCOEF, SMOOTHED

output.description: false → omit column from devc.csv (control-only device)

no_update_devc_id.description: Freeze this output when the referenced device trips

points.description: >1 → expand XBP line into N point devices (ID-01..)

node_id.description: HVAC node id(s) — 2 for NODE PRESSURE DIFFERENCE

tools.name: remove_device
tools.description: Remove a single device by ID (or internal uid). With duplicate IDs, removes only the first match.

tools.name: update_device
tools.description: Update an existing device by ID (or internal uid). Any &DEVC field can be changed; only one device is modified even with duplicate IDs.

points.description: >1 → expand XBP line into N point devices (ID-01..)

node_id.description: HVAC node id(s) — 2 for NODE PRESSURE DIFFERENCE

tools.name: add_sprinkler
tools.description: Convenience: add a complete sprinkler setup. Automatically creates DEVC (SPRINKLER LINK TEMPERATURE), PROP definition, and PART class. Just specify position and optional parameters.

tools.name: add_nozzle
tools.description: Convenience: add a Lagrangian-particle virtual fuel nozzle (e.g. hydrogen TPRD jet release). Automatically creates DEVC (QUANTITY=TIME, SETPOINT=0, ORIENTATION), PROP (MASS_FLOW_RATE / FLOW_RAMP / PARTICLE_VELOCITY / SPRAY_ANGLE / PARTICLES_PER_SECOND), PART (SPEC_ID / DIAMETER / MONODISPERSE / INITIAL_TEMPERATURE), the fuel SPEC (FORMULA + liquid-droplet properties taken from the built-in fuel database) and aligns REAC (FUEL / RADIATIVE_FRACTION / SOOT_YIELD / CO_YIELD) when no reaction is set yet.

mass_flow_rate.description: Mass flow rate at t=0 in kg/s (default 0.068)

spec_id.description: Fuel species (default 'HYDROGEN'). Known fuels get FORMULA + liquid properties automatically: HYDROGEN, METHANE, ETHANE, PROPANE, BUTANE, ETHYLENE, PROPYLENE, ACETYLENE, AMMONIA, METHANOL, ETHANOL, PROPANOL, ISOPROPANOL, ACETONE, BENZENE, TOLUENE, N-PENTANE, N-HEXANE, N-HEPTANE, N-OCTANE, ISOOCTANE, N-DECANE, DODECANE.

initial_temperature.description: Droplet initial temperature in °C (default: the fuel's boiling point −2~3°C, e.g. -255 for hydrogen)

flow_ramp_points.description: Mass-flow time series [[t,f],...] multiplying MASS_FLOW_RATE (blowdown decay etc.)

tools.name: add_heat_detector
tools.description: Convenience: add a heat detector as a small obstacle with FDS override. Generates DEVC+PROP in FDS output.

tools.name: add_smoke_detector
tools.description: Convenience: add a smoke detector as a small obstacle with FDS override. Generates DEVC+PROP in FDS output.

tools.name: add_thermocouple
tools.description: Convenience: add a thermocouple as a small obstacle with FDS override. Generates DEVC in FDS output.

tools.name: add_control
tools.description: Add a CTRL control logic element. FUNCTION_TYPE: logic ANY/ALL/NOT/XOR/X_OF_N(N), TIME_DELAY(delay), KILL/RESTART, DEADBAND(setpoint+setpoint2+on_bound), CUSTOM(ramp_id), PID(target_value+gains), math ABS/EXP/LOG/SIN/COS/ASIN/ACOS/ATAN/SUM/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY/DIVIDE/POWER/MIN/MAX (with setpoint+trip_direction they act as boolean gates). INPUT_ID accepts device IDs, other CTRL IDs, or CONSTANT.

latch.description: Allow only one state change (FDS default true; CUSTOM/PID/DEADBAND default false)

constant.description: Value used when an input is 'CONSTANT'

tools.name: update_control
tools.description: Update an existing CTRL by ID. Any field of add_control can be changed.

tools.name: remove_control
tools.description: Remove a CTRL control by ID.

tools.name: add_prop
tools.description: Add a &PROP device model. quantity presets seed standard defaults: 'LINK TEMPERATURE' (heat detector link), 'SPRINKLER LINK TEMPERATURE', 'CHAMBER OBSCURATION' (smoke detector), 'THERMOCOUPLE' (bead). Override any field. Reference from devices via prop_id.

tools.name: update_prop
tools.description: Update an existing &PROP model by ID. Same fields as add_prop.

tools.name: remove_prop
tools.description: Remove a &PROP model by ID. Devices referencing it fall back to solver defaults.

tools.name: set_mesh_cell_size
tools.description: Set a uniform cell size (m); NI/NJ/NK are computed from the current domain extents. ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

tools.name: auto_fit_mesh
tools.description: Auto-fit the mesh domain to the bounding box of all obstacles plus margin; recomputes NI/NJ/NK to keep the current cell size. ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

tools.name: set_run_options
tools.description: Set simulation RUN options (RUN dialog): solver type (gpu / gpu_cutcell = octree cut-cell engine (beta), runs on the grid from the Mesh dialog cut-cell tab / cpu_openmp), CPU thread count, FDS output path.

tools.name: set_mesh
tools.description: Set the computational mesh resolution and domain extents (a single &MESH). ⚠ Resets any multi-mesh deck to a single mesh. Use set_meshes / auto_multimesh to keep or build a multi-mesh deck.

ni.description: Number of cells in X direction

nj.description: Number of cells in Y direction

nk.description: Number of cells in Z direction

tools.name: set_time
tools.description: Set the simulation end time.

tools.name: update_dump_config
tools.description: Update output dump intervals and settings.

dt_bndf.description: Boundary (.bf) output interval (s). Omit or 0 to leave DT_BNDF out of the deck. The GPU engine writes BNDF at the DT_SLCF interval, so this only affects the CPU solver.

dt_restart.description: Restart/checkpoint interval (s). The GPU engine now writes a resumable checkpoint at this cadence.

nframes.description: FDS NFRAMES (default 1000): any DT_* left unset is filled with (T_END-T_BEGIN)/NFRAMES. Lower it to cut slice/smoke frame count and disk usage on long runs.

tools.name: set_turbulence_model
tools.description: Set the turbulence model. Options: DEARDORFF (default), VREMAN, WALE, CONSTANT_SMAGORINSKY.

tools.name: set_simulation_mode
tools.description: Set simulation mode: LES, VLES, SVLES, or DNS

tools.name: set_numerics
tools.description: Set numerical stability controls (time step and advection scheme). Use this when a run diverges, produces NaN, or when matching CPU FDS settings. dt/lock_time_step map to &TIME; the rest to &MISC. Omitted fields keep the FDS default for the current SIMULATION_MODE.

dt.description: Initial time step [s]. Omit to let the solver derive it from CFL_MAX*min(dx)/sqrt(g*H).

lock_time_step.description: Freeze dt (disable CFL adaptation). Requires dt. Standard remedy for a diverging case.

cfl_max.description: CFL upper bound (FDS VLES default 1.0). Lower it (e.g. 0.5) to stabilise.

cfl_min.description: CFL lower bound (default 0.8) — below this the solver grows dt.

vn_max.description: Von Neumann (diffusion) stability limit. VLES 1.0 / LES 0.8 / DNS 0.5.

flux_limiter.description: Scalar advection limiter. VLES default SUPERBEE, LES/DNS default CHARM. The GPU engine has no CHARM/MP5 and falls back to MINMOD with a warning.

tools.name: get_numerics
tools.description: Read the current numerical stability settings (time step, CFL/VN limits, flux limiter).

tools.name: set_ambient
tools.description: Set the ambient (initial atmosphere) conditions written to &MISC: TMPA (ambient temperature °C), HUMIDITY (%RH), Y_CO2_INFTY (background CO2 mass fraction). The GPU engine reads all three. Use `extra` for any other &MISC key you need to carry (e.g. P_INF, GVEC) — it is written verbatim. Pass null for a key to drop it and fall back to the FDS default (TMPA 20°C, HUMIDITY 40%).

extra.description: Raw &MISC entries as 'KEY=VALUE' (e.g. ["P_INF=101325."]). Replaces any entry with the same KEY.

tools.name: get_simulation_settings
tools.description: Read every simulation setting in one call: time (T_BEGIN/T_END), SIMULATION_MODE, turbulence model, numerics (DT/CFL/VN/flux limiter), ambient &MISC values, output dump intervals and Plot3D quantities, and the mesh deck size. Use it before changing settings so you know what is already explicit.

tools.name: list_raw_namelists
tools.description: List the raw namelist lines carried through unchanged (&RADI, &PRES, &COMB, &ZONE, &MULT, …) — settings the GUI has no dialog for but the deck and the engine keep.

tools.name: add_raw_namelist
tools.description: Add a raw namelist line emitted verbatim just before &TAIL — for settings with no GUI dialog (e.g. "&RADI RADIATIVE_FRACTION=0.35 /", "&PRES VELOCITY_TOLERANCE=1.E-4 /"). Must start with & and end with /. Use the dedicated tools for anything the GUI does model (&MESH/&OBST/&VENT/&SURF/&REAC/&DEVC/&CTRL/&SLCF/&BNDF/&DUMP/&TIME/&MISC) — a duplicate namelist is an FDS error.

tools.name: remove_raw_namelist
tools.description: Remove a raw namelist line by its index from list_raw_namelists.

tools.name: list_meshes
tools.description: List the current &MESH deck (multi-mesh or the single mesh) with per-mesh XB, IJK, cell size, cell count and coarse/fine ratio, plus totals and a self-check for overlap / gaps / non-cubic cells. Read this before set_meshes, slice_mesh or merge_meshes so index numbers refer to the right mesh.

tools.name: set_meshes
tools.description: Replace the whole &MESH deck with an explicit list of meshes (multi-mesh). Passing a single mesh reverts the project to single-mesh mode. config.mesh (the union bounding box) and the OPEN-boundary vents are kept consistent by the app. Engine constraints (GPU_code multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes; for shape-driven placement prefer auto_multimesh.

meshes.description: Meshes that together tile the domain, in order.

id.description: Optional mesh ID (must be unique, e.g. M1)

tools.name: slice_mesh
tools.description: Split one mesh into two at a plane (multi-mesh cutter). The coordinate snaps to that mesh's own grid lines, cell size is preserved on both halves, and OPEN vents crossing the plane are split too. Slicing the single mesh turns the project into a multi-mesh deck. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

axis.description: Axis normal to the cut plane

coord.description: Cut position (m). Snapped to the nearest grid line of that mesh.

tools.name: merge_meshes
tools.description: Merge several meshes back into one (inverse of slice_mesh). Succeeds only when the selected meshes do not overlap and their union is exactly a box. When their cell sizes differ, `choice` picks which size the result uses; the union must divide into a whole number of those cells. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

indices.description: Mesh indices to merge (2 or more)

choice.description: Cell size to keep when the meshes differ: 'coarse' (larger cells, fewer) or 'fine'.

tools.name: auto_multimesh
tools.description: Build a multi-mesh deck from the OBSTRUCTION geometry. It measures the fluid gap everywhere (obstacles minus HOLEs, so doorways stay open), gives narrow places 3+ cells across and open places the default wide cell, then merges equal-size regions into boxes cut on obstacle faces so walls stay on mesh boundaries. Wall slabs up to 2 cells thick are absorbed into a neighbour. Cell sizes are quantised to min_cell x 2^k; an overlapping, gapped or misaligned deck is refused, not committed. The domain may grow to a multiple of the coarsest cell; OPEN vents follow. Engine constraints (GPU_code multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify the result with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05. Must be > 0; it is the bottom of the 2^k ladder.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

tools.name: auto_cutcell_mesh
tools.description: Build a cut-cell multi-mesh deck from &GEOM triangulated shapes (plus OBSTs). Cells shrink where the fluid gap is narrow (gap / gap_cells), the GEOM surface band always gets the finest cell so the engine keeps its cut-cell wall physics there, sharp curvature gets one level finer, and levels change at most 2:1 between neighbouring blocks. Cell sizes are min_cell x 2^k. If the deck has no GEOM this is identical to auto_multimesh. Over budget it relaxes curvature, buffer, gap_cells, then raises min_cell and reports what it changed; a gapped, overlapping or misaligned deck is refused. Engine constraints (GPU_code multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05 — used on the GEOM surface band and in narrow gaps.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

gap_cells.description: Minimum cells across a narrow gap (default 4, floor 3).

tools.name: add_material
tools.description: Add a material definition (MATL).

tools.name: update_material
tools.description: Update a material by ID.

tools.name: remove_material
tools.description: Remove a material by ID.

tools.name: add_ramp
tools.description: Add a time ramp (RAMP) for time-dependent parameters. Points are [time, value] pairs.

tools.name: update_ramp
tools.description: Update an existing ramp with new points.

tools.name: remove_ramp
tools.description: Remove a ramp by ID.

tools.name: add_surface
tools.description: Add a general surface (&SURF) with material layers, burning behaviour, thermal boundary conditions and injection. This is what gives walls/objects real heat transfer and lets them burn away.

heat_transfer_model.description: HEAT_TRANSFER_MODEL — gas-side convective correlation. 'DEFAULT' omits the key; any other string than these is rejected by FDS.

layers.description: Material layers, outermost first. Each layer: thickness [m] + material composition (mass fractions summing to 1).

reaction_mode.description: 'material' = burning governed by MATL pyrolysis, 'manual' = governed by HRRPUA/MLRPUA on this surface

ignition.description: Burn immediately or ignite at a temperature

burn_away.description: BURN_AWAY — allow the obstruction to burn away

tools.name: update_surface
tools.description: Update an existing general surface (&SURF) by ID. Only the given fields change.

heat_transfer_model.description: HEAT_TRANSFER_MODEL — gas-side convective correlation. 'DEFAULT' omits the key; any other string than these is rejected by FDS.

layers.description: Material layers, outermost first. Each layer: thickness [m] + material composition (mass fractions summing to 1).

reaction_mode.description: 'material' = burning governed by MATL pyrolysis, 'manual' = governed by HRRPUA/MLRPUA on this surface

ignition.description: Burn immediately or ignite at a temperature

burn_away.description: BURN_AWAY — allow the obstruction to burn away

tools.name: remove_surface
tools.description: Remove a general surface (&SURF) by ID. Objects referencing it fall back to INERT.

tools.name: list_surfaces
tools.description: List all user-defined general surfaces (&SURF) with their layers and burning behaviour.

tools.name: assign_surface
tools.description: Assign a surface (SURF_ID) to an obstacle, vent or geometry. Without 'faces' the whole object uses it; with 'faces' only those faces do (SURF_ID6 order -X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z).

surf_id.description: Surface ID to assign (a user surface or a built-in like INERT/OPEN)

target_id.description: ID of the obstacle / vent / geom

faces.description: Obstacle faces only: 'xn','xp','yn','yp','zn','zp' (-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z). Omit for all faces.

tools.name: list_material_library
tools.description: List built-in material presets (density/conductivity/specific heat/pyrolysis) available to add to the model, optionally filtered by category or search text.

category.description: Filter: structure, wood, insulation, plastic, textile, cable, liquid_fuel, metal, other

search.description: Substring match on id / Korean / English name

tools.name: add_material_from_library
tools.description: Copy a material preset from the built-in library into the model as a &MATL.

id.description: Optional new ID in the model (defaults to the library ID)

tools.name: add_surface_from_library
tools.description: Copy a surface preset from the built-in library into the model as a &SURF, pulling in any materials it needs.

library_id.description: Library surface ID (see the Surfaces library in the GUI)

id.description: Optional new ID in the model (defaults to the library ID)

tools.name: list_slcf
tools.description: List all slice (SLCF) outputs with id, quantity, plane, and flags.

tools.name: set_plot3d_outputs
tools.description: Set the Plot3D output quantities and species IDs (NUM dialog). Provide up to 5 quantities.

spec_ids.description: Species IDs for VOLUME FRACTION quantities

tools.name: add_slcf
tools.description: Add a slice file output (SLCF). Specify quantity and plane position.

quantity.description: Quantity: TEMPERATURE, VELOCITY, VISIBILITY, VOLUME FRACTION, etc.

spec_id.description: Species ID for VOLUME FRACTION quantity

tools.name: remove_slcf
tools.description: Remove a slice file output by ID.

tools.name: update_slcf
tools.description: Update an existing SLCF output by ID.

tools.name: list_bndf
tools.description: List the animated boundary (BNDF) quantities written for solid surfaces.

tools.name: add_bndf
tools.description: Add an animated boundary quantity (&BNDF) such as WALL TEMPERATURE or ADIABATIC SURFACE TEMPERATURE. Use spec_id for species quantities (MASS FLUX, SURFACE DEPOSITION, MPUA_Z, CPUA_Z, AMPUA_Z) and part_id for particle quantities (MPUA, CPUA, AMPUA). The GPU engine records these 7 quantities: WALL TEMPERATURE, WALL HEAT FLUX, NET HEAT FLUX, RADIATIVE HEAT FLUX, CONVECTIVE HEAT FLUX, INCIDENT HEAT FLUX, BACK WALL TEMPERATURE. Any other quantity needs CPU FDS (the GPU engine warns and falls back to WALL HEAT FLUX). WALL HEAT FLUX is a GPU-engine-only name — use NET HEAT FLUX when the deck must also run on CPU FDS.

part_id.description: Particle class ID, for particle-based quantities

tools.name: remove_bndf
tools.description: Remove an animated boundary quantity (&BNDF) by QUANTITY (and SPEC_ID/PART_ID when the entry has one).

tools.name: set_chid
tools.description: Set the simulation CHID (Case Heading Identifier) and optional title. Note: when the project is saved, CHID is normalized to the .fds file name (so output files such as <name>.smv match the deck file); a CHID set here only persists until the next save.

chid.description: Case ID (no spaces, used for output filenames)

tools.name: preview_fds
tools.description: Render the current project as FDS deck text and return it WITHOUT writing a file (the GUI FDS Preview dialog). Use `namelist` to show only one group (e.g. "MESH", "SLCF", "OBST", "DUMP") and `max_lines` to cap the output. This is the fastest way to check that a mesh / output / geometry change lands in the deck the way you expect.

namelist.description: Show only this namelist group, without '&' (e.g. MESH, DUMP, SLCF, OBST, VENT, SURF, CTRL)

max_lines.description: Maximum lines to return (default 200; the reply says how many were cut)

tools.name: validate_project
tools.description: Pre-flight check of the whole project before export or run: deck generation, mesh/domain sanity, objects outside the domain, duplicate IDs, dangling SURF_ID / MATL_ID / CTRL INPUT_ID / DEVC references, output intervals larger than T_END (which would store only the t=0 frame), missing OPEN boundary, fire without a reaction fuel, and LOCK_TIME_STEP without DT. Returns errors (deck will not run) and warnings (deck runs but the result is probably not what you want).

tools.name: rewrite_fds_via_ai
tools.description: FALLBACK for requests no dedicated tool can express (complex multi-mesh layouts, bulk or unusual namelist edits, anything the other tools cannot do). It exports the whole current project as a complete .fds file, sends the file plus your `instruction` to the AI model acting as an FDS editor, validates the edited file, and applies only the sections that changed back to the project (untouched sections keep their GUI metadata). Write `instruction` as a precise, self-contained editing brief in FDS terms (namelists, IDs, XB coordinates, IJK, cell sizes) — e.g. "Split the single &MESH into 4 meshes along x with cell size 0.1 m, keep the domain" or "Add &MULT-free 2×2 mesh grid, meshes must align". Do NOT use it for things a dedicated tool already does (add_wall, set_mesh, auto_multimesh, ...).

instruction.description: Exact editing brief for the FDS file (what to change, where, with which values).

tools.name: shape_add_arch
tools.description: Shape Studio: add an ARCHED / VAULTED / SEMICIRCULAR ceiling (barrel vault, dome-roof tunnel) in ONE call — a curved shell whose inner surface is a circular arc of clear width `span` and inner height `rise` above the springing line (rise = span/2 → semicircle; smaller → shallow segmental arch), extruded `length` metres along `axis`. Use this whenever the user asks for a round/arched/curved/semicircular ceiling or tunnel roof instead of composing primitives. Placement: `start` = coordinate along the axis where the arch begins, `center` = transverse coordinate of the arch centre line, `z_base` = height of the springing line (0 = arch rises from the floor; for a room use the wall-top height). Afterwards export it with shape_export_geom (exact curved &GEOM for the cut-cell solver) or shape_export_obst (voxelised). Units: metres.

span.description: Inner clear width (m), e.g. tunnel width

rise.description: Inner arch height above the springing line (m). Default span/2 (semicircle).

start.description: Axis coordinate where the arch begins (m). Default 0

center.description: Transverse coordinate of the arch centre line (m). Default 0

tools.description: Shape Studio: boolean of nodes. union=merge all; subtract=first minus rest; intersect=common volume. Input nodes are consumed into the result.

tools.name: shape_transform

tools.name: shape_array

tools.name: shape_hull

tools.name: shape_set_params

params.description: Partial node params to merge (same keys as creation)

tools.name: shape_edit_node
tools.description: Shape Studio: rename / show-hide / assign FDS SURF / set color / mark fire faces + fire properties of a node. fire_faces: 6 booleans in FDS SURF_ID6 order [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] OR face-name strings like ["-Z"] ("bottom"/"top" aliases ok); [] clears. Fire faces render as red hatching in the viewport and are wired to a FIRE SURF (+ RAMP_Q / &REAC) on shape_export_obst. Fire properties (merged individually, unspecified keys keep their previous value): fire_hrrpua, fire_tmp_front (°C), fire_ramp_points ([[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...] HRR time curve), fire_fuel_type, fire_soot_yield, fire_co_yield, fire_radiative_fraction, fire_ext_coeff. ONE FIRE OBST PER DOCUMENT: fire faces may exist on only one shape — assigning them to another node automatically clears the previous node's fire faces. PLAN FIRST: real FDS can only apply a fire SURF to a FLAT face (never a curved or stepped one), so setting fire_faces without plan_confirmed changes nothing (the fire_* properties in the same call are dropped too) and returns a 6-direction flatness analysis instead — discuss it with the user, agree on which flat face, HRRPUA, RAMP and combustion properties, then call again with plan_confirmed=true.

fire_faces.description: [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] booleans or face names, [] to clear. Only ONE node per document may have fire faces (others are cleared automatically)

fire_hrrpua.description: Fire face HRRPUA kW/m² (default 1000 at export)

fire_ramp_points.description: HRR time curve for RAMP_Q: [[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...]

fire_fuel_type.description: Fuel PRESET id — WOOD_OAK, POLYURETHANE_FOAM, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE. Prefer a preset id: export then writes &REAC FUEL plus the matching C/H/O/N, soot/CO yield and radiative fraction. Any other string is passed through as a raw FUEL name with no chemistry.

plan_confirmed.description: Set true only AFTER the user agreed on the flat fire face and the fire properties (required to actually apply fire_faces and the fire_* properties sent with it)

tools.name: shape_delete_node
tools.description: Shape Studio: delete a node. with_inputs (default true) also deletes its consumed input subtree.

tools.name: shape_undo
tools.description: Shape Studio: undo the last document mutation.

tools.name: shape_export_obst
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS: voxelize the shape (node_id, or union of all visible roots) and add it to the model as an obstacle with voxel geometry. voxel_size in m (e.g. 0.1). origin optionally repositions the bbox min corner in the domain.

node_id.description: Node to export (default: union of visible roots)

origin.description: Domain position of bbox min corner (default: keep authored coords)

surf_id.description: SURF for all faces (default: node surf or INERT)

tools.name: shape_export_geom
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS cut-cell: export the exact CSG mesh as an &GEOM triangulated surface — no voxelization, so slopes and curves keep their true shape instead of being stair-stepped like shape_export_obst. Only a watertight surface is exported: primitives, hull, array, mirror and non-overlapping unions are fine, but an OVERLAPPING boolean (union/subtract/intersect) always leaves an open seam the CSG library cannot close, so the export is refused — voxelize those with shape_export_obst instead. Needs a GPU engine build with cut-cell support; older engines parse &GEOM but ignore it. Fire (HRRPUA) on a GEOM surface is not supported yet — use shape_export_obst for the burner. Units m, z-up. Default: every visible root, each keeping its own SURF; origin repositions the bbox min corner.

geom_id.description: New &GEOM ID (re-exporting with the same ID replaces it)

node_id.description: Node to export (default: union of visible roots, per-node SURF kept)

surf_id.description: SURF for all faces (default: per-node SURF, else FDS default surface)

origin.description: Domain position of bbox min corner (default: keep authored coords)

rgb.description: Display colour 0-255 (default: let Smokeview use the SURF colour)

allow_open.description: Write the &GEOM even when the surface has holes. Not recommended: FDS stops with ERROR(730) and the GPU cut-cell solver mis-classifies inside/outside

tools.name: shape_export_stl
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD (OpenFOAM etc.): export the exact CSG mesh as STL (no voxelization). ascii=true for text STL with solid name (snappyHexMesh patch name). Units m, z-up.

tools.name: shape_export_obj
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD: export the exact CSG mesh as OBJ (no voxelization). Units m, z-up.

node_id.description: Node to register (default: union of visible roots)

tools.name: shape_preview_voxels
tools.description: Shape Studio: switch the viewport into FDS voxel preview mode — it shows exactly what the shape becomes once voxelized into FDS OBST boxes (including the fire faces). size = voxel edge in metres (default 0.1), off=true returns to the smooth CSG view. Call this before shape_screenshot to review the FDS result rather than the ideal mesh. GUI only (no effect headless).
